note: Research only. No task edits the quote store, the site, the tools, or CI. Every task writes exactly one report under research/ and proves it with an acceptance command. engine/model/bounds are deliberately left for the coordinator to pin: no live worker experiment or paid model benchmark runs without an explicit provider, model, budget and Stu's approval.

defaults.commit_instruction: One commit on the worker branch containing only the report file. Do not merge, do not push to main, do not open a PR — the coordinator decides what is adopted.

bounds.network: read-only HTTP GET; no form submissions, no account creation, no purchases

boundaries: Read-only outside research/: no edits to the store, the site, the tools or CI, and no commits to main.
Never present a model's wording as a source's wording. If you cannot fetch it, it is not evidence.
No accounts, no purchases, no form submissions, no rate-limit evasion.

tasks.title: Fallback sources for his first-person posts
tasks.question: If the trumpstruth.org archive feed disappeared tomorrow, which other public sources carry the same posts, and how do their ids map to the canonical truthsocial.com post URL?
tasks.why: That feed is currently the only automated path for first-person posts, so it is a single point of failure for the whole store.
must_include: at least three candidates, each probed with a real HTTP request and its status recorded
for each: does it carry the canonical truthsocial.com URL or original id, or only its own id?
stability signals: who runs it, is there robots.txt, does it rate-limit
a ranked recommendation with the trade-off stated, including 'do not use' where the route requires disguising the client
boundaries: Do not fetch truthsocial.com itself with a spoofed browser User-Agent. If a source only works that way, record that as the finding and disqualify it.
Record failures as findings (dead, blocked, paywalled), do not route around them.

tasks.title: How reliable is verbatim X post resolution?
tasks.question: Given a post id, which public resolvers return the verbatim post text, and at what success rate and rate limit?
tasks.why: The X route depends on a verifier supplying the words; if it is flaky, every X candidate silently drops.
must_include: a sample of at least 10 real post ids (source them however you like — search engines, public pages — as long as each id is real and you say where it came from)
per resolver: success count, failures with the exact error, latency, and any rate limit you observed
what each resolver does with a deleted or protected post (this is the honesty case: it must fail, not invent)
a recommended fallback chain
boundaries: Never present a model's paraphrase of a post as the post text.
No API keys, no accounts, no paid tiers.

tasks.title: Is the news-quote extractor worth its candidates?
tasks.question: Across a labelled sample, what is the precision of the sentence-quote extractor in tools/ingest.mjs, and what single change would raise it most?
tasks.why: Every false positive costs a human review and weakens the claim that a candidate is a quote with a receipt.
must_include: a labelled sample of at least 25 candidates produced by the extractor, each marked correct / wrong / unclear, with the reason for each wrong one
the measured precision, with the sample size stated
failure modes grouped (e.g. quote belongs to another speaker, headline fragment, paraphrase in quotes)
one recommended change with its expected effect, plus a fixture file under research/fixtures/ that would test it
boundaries: Do not modify tools/ingest.mjs. Propose; do not implement.
Run the extractor read-only if you use it; do not write to data/candidates/.

tasks.title: What may a public site legally reproduce here?
tasks.question: For a public, non-commercial site that shows one short quote at a time with a source link, what are the actual constraints — copyright, personality/image rights, and the terms of the services the pipeline reads?
tasks.why: The site is going public on a custom domain. This is the one risk nobody has looked at yet.
must_include: copyright position on short quotations with attribution, including any jurisdiction-relevant doctrine, cited to a real source
name/image/trademark considerations for the site's branding
the terms of service of: truthsocial.com, x.com, trumpstruth.org, and any mirror recommended by task-01 — specifically what they say about automated reading and redistribution
a pragmatic risk list: what is fine, what needs a change, what needs a human lawyer
boundaries: This is not legal advice and the report must say so plainly in its first paragraph.
Cite primary sources (the actual terms pages), not blog summaries.

tasks.title: Upgrade the twelve legacy quotes or declare them unfindable
tasks.question: For each of the twelve quotes migrated from the 2018 demo, is there a real primary or secondary source that pins it — and if not, which should be retired from a site that promises a receipt?
tasks.why: Eight of the twelve are labelled 'widely reported — no located primary source'. The site's credibility rests on that label being temporary rather than permanent.
must_include: one row per quote id (see data/quotes/ for the twelve), with: found source URL, source type (primary/secondary/reference) and a verbatim excerpt proving the wording
for the ones you cannot pin: what you searched, and a recommendation to retire, keep labelled, or keep hunting
explicitly flag any quote whose wording appears to have drifted from what the source says
boundaries: Do not edit data/quotes/ — this is a proposal table for a human to apply.
Do not invent a source. 'Unfindable' is a valuable result; a plausible-looking citation is a disaster.
Wikipedia alone does not upgrade a quote above 'widely reported' — find the underlying transcript, video or report.

tasks.title: What does legitimate X automation cost, today?
tasks.question: Ignoring scraper workarounds, what are the real options and current prices for reading @realDonaldTrump's posts programmatically?
tasks.why: Everything currently leans on a Grok Bot handoff. That is fine but it is one path, and nobody has priced the alternatives.
must_include: each option with its current price, cited to the vendor's own pricing page and dated
what each tier actually permits (read access to another account's timeline? volume? commercial use?)
xAI API live search: price per search, and whether it returns post ids or only prose answers
a monthly cost estimate for this project's realistic volume (tens of posts a day, not millions)
a recommendation: stay as we are, or change, and what would change it
boundaries: No purchases, no account creation, no free-trial signups.
Prices change: state the date you read them and link the page.
